Definition: to crack off, i.e. (figuratively) burst out in rage
BiblicalUsage: To burst out in rage is the word for God's anger and His people's plea: the LORD heard the voice of your words, and was wroth, and sware. Isaiah says, behold, Thou art wroth, for we have sinned; and again, be not wroth very sore, O LORD, neither remember iniquity for ever.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the wrath is real and the plea is real, and the same word holds them together: God is wroth because we sinned, and we ask Him not to be wroth for ever. That is the whole of the gospel in two verses, and I hold to it.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
